title: n8n customer-agent tool catalog
description: The format of catalog.json. Validate with `ajv validate -s tool.schema.json -d catalog.json`. This schema is the contract between the backend (which owns the endpoints) and the n8n MCP configuration (which owns the agent). It is deliberately free of n8n vocabulary: nothing here names a node, a credential or a workflow, so the same catalog drives a different orchestrator without edits.

catalog_version.description: Semver. PATCH = wording. MINOR = tools added, or an optional parameter added. MAJOR = a tool renamed or removed, a required parameter added, or a response shape changed.

source_of_truth.description: Repo-relative path to the api-doc tree these tools were derived from.

defaults.description: Shared values every tool inherits, so no tool repeats a base URL or a header. A tool may override any of these.

surfaces.description: An access surface: how a tool reaches the backend, and what credential it carries.

identity.description: messaging_identity_required: the call MUST carry the resolved messaging identity envelope and the backend resolves the customer from it. A customer id, user id or access token is NEVER a tool parameter.

identity_envelope.description: The shape every identity-bearing call carries, documented once here rather than repeated in every tool's parameters.

name.description: Stable identifier, shaped `domain_verb_object`. Never renamed in place: a rename is a MAJOR catalog version.

title.description: Short human label for dashboards and logs. Not read by the model.

tier.description: core: always in the model's tool list. extended: loaded on demand, once the conversation is already in that domain. flow_only: NEVER exposed to the model, callable only by a deterministic flow step. Money, destructive and credential-adjacent operations live here.

status.description: available: the endpoint exists today and was verified against the source. gap: it does not exist and must be built before this tool can be configured.

gap_ref.description: Which piece of planned work introduced this tool. GAP-nnn is BACKEND-GAPS.md; MCP-PARITY-n is a step of MCP-PARITY-PLAN.md. ⚠ The second form was added 2026-09-06, after steps 1-3 had already written ten rows the old pattern refused — nothing validates this file today, so the drift was silent.

description.description: Written FOR the model, describing what the customer gets. Not an HTTP description.

when_not_to_use.description: The highest-leverage field for selection accuracy. Name the tool that should be used instead.

path.description: Path template; `{name}` placeholders are filled from parameters via request.path.

command.description: CommandBus command name, for webhook_command tools only. It may differ from what the user types: `reset_password` against `/reset-password`.

backing_endpoint.description: The customer-facing endpoint this tool is equivalent to, when the tool goes through the bot surface rather than calling it directly. This field is what makes drift detectable: if the referenced api-doc changes and the tool does not, the catalog is stale.

parameters.description: A single JSON Schema for everything the model supplies. ONE flat object: the model must never be asked to know which value is a path segment, which is a query string and which is a body field. `request` does that mapping.

request.description: Where each parameter goes on the wire.

body_literal.description: Fixed body fields the model does not supply.

source.description: Where the payload sits. Most jovi-mall routes use the {success,data} envelope; the bot webhook and the three payment routes deliberately do not.

important_fields.description: The fields the model should actually receive. Everything else is dropped before the model sees it — a full product detail is several kB of noise around six useful values.

never_relay.description: Fields that must never be echoed into the chat OR written to the conversation transcript.

result_kind.description: Key into the normalized result vocabulary; decides which platform renderer runs. See ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.

customer_action.description: A closed vocabulary, so every tool's failures are handled uniformly. Semantics in errors.json.

details_fields.description: Fields inside error.details worth putting into the customer-facing sentence.

idempotency.description: How repeat safety is achieved, or why it is absent.

requires_confirmation.description: false: execute directly. true: two-phase confirmation echoing the resolved subject. out_of_band: never confirmed or executed in chat — emit a link and let the customer complete it on the web.

context_resolution.description: How this tool's subject may be resolved from conversation context rather than an explicit identifier. See ARCHITECTURE.md section 7.

must_echo.description: true: the resolved subject must be named back to the customer before or with the result.

requires_customer_role.description: true: refuse when the resolved sender holds no customer role. A vendor, agency or agent messaging the bot must not reach it.

commands.description: Command names in commands.json that reach this tool.
